Thanks for the clear ask, Daniel — copied my summary and next steps below. I've attached a redline to their proposed amendment (file: redlined_dpa_karthik_20260412.docx). High-level notes: 

1) Subprocessors — Accept list of three additions. We'll add an "Exhibit: Subprocessors (EU)" that enumerates the three companies. For operational hygiene, we request:
   - Lumina to represent that each subprocessor maintains at least one industry-recognized control (SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001); evidence provided on request.
   - Redwood to provide a 30-day notice for any future subprocessor additions, with Lumina having a 10-day objection window. If Lumina objects, we'll use the standard mitigation / alternative hosting discussion.

2) Data transfers — We can adopt an SCC exhibit. Proposed language: Redwood to effect transfers relying on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) appended as an Exhibit, and Redwood will maintain a mechanism to ensure subprocessors are bound accordingly. We will not agree to an open-ended "global transfer mechanism" without the SCC anchoring.

3) Retention & deletion — We'll add a one-paragraph exhibit limiting retention for Lumina-derived activity logs to 13 months (unless otherwise agreed) and reaffirm the data deletion process in Section 6.

4) Execution — We can do a re-execution by DocuSign once redlines are accepted. Please confirm the Lumina signature party and signatory authority (legal/procurement).

Next steps: We are returning a redlined amendment by end of day (attached). Karthik, if you can confirm turnaround expectations with Lumina, we'll prepare a clean amendment and queue a DocuSign envelope.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
